review_notes: I read all three declarations in the target (lines 1–177): `rnDeriv_le_of_le_smul`, `endpointCoupling_couples` and `CurvatureDimension.reroute_finite_subplan`. I then searched the OAI WeakHessian tree for proofs that repeat the same reasoning. The main proof, lines 79–170, is reproduced almost line for line in `CurvatureDimension.reroute_finite_subplan_short` in Transport/RerouteFiniteSubplanShort.lean. The only real difference is where the path-length bound `hlen` comes from. The step that rescales an optimal plan back to the mass of θ, matching its endpoint marginals and its cost bound (lines 137–160), also appears a third time in `OptimalPlansShort.subplan` in Transport/OptimalPlansShort.lean. Both downstream files use `endpointCoupling_couples` and `rnDeriv_le_of_le_smul` from the target, so they depend on it. Any shared helper therefore has to live in the target file or below it, and it cannot use the later `OptimalPlansShort` definition; I wrote the helper's length hypothesis out in full for that reason. I did not count the timeZero/timeOne mirror blocks inside the single proof (hd0/hd1, hb0/hb1, hπ0/hπ1) as separate findings. I also skipped the repeated measurability fact for `(γ timeZero, γ timeOne)`, because it is a one-line routine fact. I could not compile anything, so the proposed rewrites and proof sketches are untested. One open question is whether `simp`/`change` steps will need small adjustments once the code moves into a lemma with explicit `q`.

findings.problem: Three proofs repeat the same step: after scaling an optimal plan η for the normalised measure q⁻¹ • θ back by q, they show that q • η has the same endpoint marginals as θ and an endpoint-coupling cost no larger than θ's. Each proof does this with a local `hξend` (map_smul / `change` / `hcanc`) and a local `hs` that pulls the scalar out of `QuadraticTransportCost (endpointCoupling (q • η))`, then combines them with `mul_le_mul'` and `hopt.2 … (endpointCoupling_couples θ')`. The copies are here (lines 140–160), in `reroute_finite_subplan_short` (lines 115–134) and in `OptimalPlansShort.subplan` (lines 253–272). The third copy is in a separate lemma, so it remains even if the first finding is adopted.
findings.proposed_change:
Add the following lemma to this file, after `endpointCoupling_couples`:

lemma IsOptimalCoupling.smul_rescale {θ η : Measure (Curve X)} {q : ℝ≥0∞} (hq : q ≠ 0) (hqt : q ≠ ∞) (hopt : IsOptimalCoupling (endpointCoupling η) (interpolation (q⁻¹ • θ) timeZero) (interpolation (q⁻¹ • θ) timeOne)) : interpolation (q • η) timeZero = interpolation θ timeZero ∧ interpolation (q • η) timeOne = interpolation θ timeOne ∧ QuadraticTransportCost (endpointCoupling (q • η)) ≤ QuadraticTransportCost (endpointCoupling θ)

Proof sketch: `hcanc : q • (q⁻¹ • θ) = θ` by `smul_smul`, `ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel hq hqt` and `one_smul`. The endpoint equalities follow from `Measure.map_smul` together with `hopt.1.interpolation_endpoints` (the current `hξend` body). For the cost, use the scalar-extraction identity (the current `hs`, via `Measure.map_smul` and `lintegral_smul_measure`) and `mul_le_mul' le_rfl (hopt.2 _ (endpointCoupling_couples (q⁻¹ • θ)))`, then rewrite with `hcanc`.

Rewritten uses:
- Here: `obtain ⟨hξ0, hξ1, hcost⟩ := hopt.smul_rescale (θ := θ) hq hqt`. Then `refine ⟨ξ, hξfin, hξmass, …, hξ0, hξ1, hcost, ?_⟩`, which removes lines 140–147 and 150–160.
- In `OptimalPlansShort.subplan`: `obtain ⟨hξ0, hξ1, hcost⟩ := hoη.smul_rescale hq hqt`, which replaces lines 253–272. The hypotheses `hq : θ univ ≠ 0` and `hqt` are already in scope there, and θ' is definitionally `q⁻¹ • θ`.
findings.benefit: The rescaling step is a single mathematical fact: scaling an optimal plan for a normalised sub-plan back by q gives a competitor plan with the same endpoints and no larger cost. A named lemma states that fact once and removes about twenty lines of `change`/`map_smul` work from each of three proofs. It also leaves one place to update if the definitions of `interpolation` or `endpointCoupling` change.
